KN5000-family inventory, measured read-only on 2026-10-24. I hashed every copy with sha1sum (list in /home/fsanches/compartilhado/tmp/technics-audit-inventory-kn5000/sha1.txt and romfiles.sha1) and compared it with the repo's original_ROMs/. 44 files are tracked under original_ROMs/, 75,467,058 B (`git ls-files original_ROMs | du -cb`). Note that this repo has a public GitHub remote (ArqueologiaDigital/technics-roms-disasm), while technics_roms/README.md says its own contents must never be published.

Three source copies hold identical bytes wherever their filenames match: ~/compartilhado/kn5000_original_roms, technics_roms/roms/kn5000 and the repo. technics_romsets/kn5000 and kn5000_corrected_roms are symlink farms. The only real file in kn5000_corrected_roms is the descrambled IC14 rhythm ROM, sha1 fef7f192, which equals technics_roms' current IC14. So "corrected" means the official chip content with the A19/A21 address-swap fixed. It is not homebrew.

Source-built and byte-exact in the repo (Makefile + compare_roms.py): main program v10/v9/v7, sub-CPU payload v142 plus its compressed update image, sub-CPU boot ROM IC30, table data, custom data IC19 and HD-AE5000 v2.06i. Measured with `python3 scripts/analysis/kn5000_source_coverage.py`, every one of these is 100.0% source except v7 (99.7%, 6,591 B left as raw blob) and table data (84.8%, 318,468 B left as raw blob). The "Not .incbin" percentages in CLAUDE.md are an older, different metric.

Present on disk but never built:
- Program ROMs v5, v6 and v8 are on disk but not in the repo at all. v8 differs from v9 by exactly 1 byte, at 0xFFFFE8: 0x08 instead of 0x09 (`cmp -l`). That byte is the version byte in all six releases.
- Sub-CPU payloads v140 and v141, and their compressed images, are tracked in original_ROMs but nothing in the Makefile references them. Only analysis scripts read them. Issue kn5000-v41 (build a v141 source tree) is open.
- The table-data chip halves, ic3/ic1, are tracked, but the build uses kn5000_table_data.rom. I verified that file is a 16-bit-word interleave of ic3 then ic1.
- HD-AE5000 v1.10i, v1.15i and v2.01i are not in the repo.
- Rhythm ROM IC14 and waveform ROM IC307 are not in the repo. Only analysis probes read IC307.

Duplicate: the unversioned hd-ae5000.ic4 is byte-identical to v1.15i (sha1 581fa58e). It is also identical to HKEXTROM.XAP inside the official Technics installer AE5-115.exe (ca-software-mirror/files/5000/files/ae5-115.zip).

Official update media:
- ca-software-mirror/files/5000/files/kn5-10.zip contains KN5VA.exe (dated 2004-03-19), which holds HKMSPRG.SLD. That file contains two compressed streams. I decoded them with my own decompressor: the first decodes exactly to kn5000_v10_program.rom (sha1 1f2abc5b). The second is byte-identical to kn5000_subprogram_v142_compressed.rom (sha1 13718900).
- kn5000_project/kn5000_v10_disk.img (sha1 a892bedc) is a floppy image holding the same four files with identical hashes. It is git-ignored in kn5000_project.
- Neither installer is stored in technics_roms or in this repo. No update disk for v5–v9 exists anywhere on this machine. I searched for the in-file signatures in files under 6 MB and listed the members of every .zip/.exe archive.

Floppies (all 14 KN5000 disks are data only):
- The 14 kn5000_flop disks hold 355 files in total: style data (.CMP/.LSW/.PMT/.SQT/.TM), 21 .BMP wallpapers, 12 _INHALT.TXT index files and one .RCM. None is executable and none carries a firmware signature.
- 13 of the 14 images in technics_romsets/kn5000_flop are the OLD builds. Their CRCs match the pre-rebuild softlist (hash/kn5000_flop.xml in mame-pr and its kn7000 branches). The 2026-10-18 rebuild (floppy-rebuild-2026-10-18, KN7000/technics-kn-flop-rebuild-files, and mame/hash/kn5000_flop.xml) has different hashes. Only idd5000 (crc 04e7983f) matches both.
- KN7000/floppy-archive holds KN7000 style data, not KN5000.

Hazards:
- kn5000_original_roms/kn5000/kn5000_waveform_rom.ic304/.ic305/.ic306 are the project's own synthetic placeholders, sha1 0f9b0375 / f56c7a87 / bc7f0db8. Those equal technics_roms/roms/kn5000/synthetic/SYNTHETIC_wave_placeholder_bank1/2/3. They still carry chip-dump names there and through kn5000_corrected_roms' symlinks. The repo script scripts/generators/generate_synthetic_waveforms.py still writes files under those names.
- The repo's reference driver mame_driver/src/mame/matsushita/kn5000.cpp declares IC14 as the as-read image (CRC 76d11a5e, SHA1 e4b572d3). The live fork (~/compartilhado/mame) and technics_romsets now use the descrambled one (CRC aa4917ce, SHA1 fef7f192).
- analysis/binclude-audit-2026-08-07/PLAN.md line 29 calls compressed v140 "the only copy of v1.40 ... no decompressed reference anywhere". That is wrong: technics_roms commit e86b23e (2026-07-20) already held an identical kn5000_subprogram_v140.rom (sha1 b7f47152).
- ~/compartilhado/kn5000_custom_data_with_preset.ic19 is a synthetic file, not a dump. It is IC19 with the 27,967-byte compressed preset block pasted in at offset 0xE0000. `cmp -l` shows 27,699 differing bytes, all between 0xE0000 and 0xE6D3E.

- ~/compartilhado/custom-kn5000-roms is a git repo of 24 tracked files: sources and build files only, no ROM binaries.
- The four zips in kn5000_original_roms (at_keybc, ct486, et4000, kb_ms_natural) are PC-hardware ROMs, unrelated to the KN5000.

Inventory of the non-KN5000 Technics material on this machine, checked against technics-roms-disasm at HEAD 14aec1197. Nothing was edited inside any git repo. Scratch output is in /home/fsanches/compartilhado/tmp/technics-audit-inventory-other-models/ (interleave.py, similar.py, *.sym, offmap_*.txt). Copied ROM bytes were deleted from there afterwards; it holds 680 KB now.

CPU per program image:
- KN6000, KN6500, KN2400 and the HD-SX3 card are all Panasonic MN10300 (MILK) machines. The program images carry the banner "MILK MN10300 Ver1.0R1" (KN6000 at file 0x3F77E8, KN6500 at 0x381448, KN2400 at 0x1E41AC). The HD-SX3 card has no banner; it was decoded as MN10300 with unidasm.
- KN1500 and WSA1R use the Toshiba TMP95C061 (TLCS-900). This is stated in the MAME drivers. KN1500 has a TLCS-900 vector table at 0xFFFF00, with reset at 0xFFFEE0.

Already in the repo:
- WSA1R is done, byte-exact: wsa1/, 1,311 tracked files, all four OS v2 dumps committed. Their md5s equal technics_roms/roms/wsa1.
- KN7000 is a byte-exact skeleton for program 941 / table 84 (src/program.s still holds 2,603 .incbin_range lines). The latest row of notes/coverage-history.tsv (2026-10-18) says real source is 3.88%. Also done: SP7001 942 / 83 plus BASEEXT.XAP, IC19 (100 JPEGs committed, 2,093,050 B), and the 7 .CNV converters, fully disassembled.

KN7000 builds not in the repo:
- Program 935 (v1.5).
- Program 893 (v1.3, Felipe's own chip read).
- Program 929: only the upper half survives.
- Table 80: identical to SP7001 table 83's first 0x3E0660 bytes except one byte, the build string at 0x139EE9 ('0' vs '3').
- The IC18 boot ROM: the first 64 KB of c3cbnd000046.ic18, MN10300 code. Nothing in kn7000/ disassembles or builds it.

Other models (KN6000, KN6500, KN2400/KN2600, KN1500, HD-SX3/SX6) have no folder in the repo. Small pieces exist elsewhere in it:
- kn7000/dsp/cross-model/kn6000: the KN6000 effects-DSP records, 81 files.
- kn7000/src/cnv/technics_kn6000.s.
- notes/feature-presentation-cues-probes/kn6000_*.py.
- dsp/tools/kn1500_*.py: a uPD6383 microcode corpus taken from IC15.

Every disk program image now regenerates with tools the repo already has, without DOSBox:
1. kn7000/tools/sfx_extract.py reads the zip appended to each update installer. The six .SLD files it got out of the KN6000/KN6500/KN2400 installers have the same md5 as technics_roms/sources.
2. sld_decompress.py decompresses them.
3. smck_check.py checks the result. KN6000 matches 16/16 blocks, KN6500 15/15 and KN2400 15/15, with exact totals.
4. The HD-SX3 card image hd-sx3_v1_1.bin (md5 32ca36c8...) is exactly EXTAPR.SLD from KN6000/ca_software_files/sx6-113.zip, sx6v113a.exe, decompressed to 0xC0000 bytes.

This makes two claims in technics_roms/README.md wrong:
- §4 says ".exe to .SLD is NOT scripted; the installer must be run under DOSBox". Python's zipfile does it.
- "Still undumped" lists the KN7000 wave ROMs, rhythm ROM and picture flash. All three were read from Felipe's unit in passes 2 to 4.

Two more facts about that private repo: roms/hdsx3/ is untracked there although MANIFEST.tsv lists it, and nothing in its README covers HD-SX3 or KN1500.

Running gen_symbols.py on the other program images (output to scratch only) finds function names in the MILK reflection tables:
- KN6000: 1,293 names at link base 0x4C000000, 1,007 of them also in KN7000.
- KN6500: 1,434 names at 0x4C000000, 1,142 shared.
- KN2400: 2,471 names at 0x48400000, 2,133 shared.
- HD-SX3: 98 names at 0x97800000.
- At the other base, KN6000 and KN6500 give 0 names, and so does KN2400 at 0x4C000000.

Floppy sets:
- WSA1R: 9 disks, 121 files, 7,834,534 B, all data. Nothing in the repo refers to them.
- KN7000: 6 disks. Only scd7000 holds programs, and those are done. custom1/custom2/idd7000 hold .AST files: raw deflate at +0x10 that inflates to the custom-data images (1,966,080 B, byte-equal, checked).
- KN6000: 21 disks. Only scd6000 holds programs, and those are done.

Cheapest route per missing model:
- KN6000, KN6500, KN2400 and HD-SX3 are regenerable from manufacturer update disks. Follow the kn7000/ convention: git-ignored baserom/, rebuilt by a Makefile from the installers, and a kn7asm.py source with .mnbase plus a single .incbin_range, so it matches 100% from day one. Then run gen_symbols.py.
- KN7000 935 and 893 are best ported from 941 with offset_map.py, port_symbols.py and gen_program_s.py --profile, as was done for SP7001. Their reference images must come from the private romset, as SP7001's do.
- KN1500 could reuse the wsa1/ LLVM TLCS-900 toolchain. But IC15 is a defective dump: 4 of its 8 blocks of 256 KiB have every odd byte 0xFF. Any skeleton would only reproduce a bad dump; it needs a re-dump first.
- Copyright convention in this PUBLIC repo (origin github.com/ArqueologiaDigital/technics-roms-disasm): KN5000 and WSA1 dumps are committed (44 + 8 files, 111,099,585 B including the unidasm listings). kn7000/ keeps baserom/*.rom|bin|sld|inf|xap|img git-ignored. top_gaps.title: 1. Routine header comments are missing on most call targets in the maincpu trees and HD-AE5000
top_gaps.detail: Call targets with no ';' comment block directly above them: v10 4,397 of 5,320 (82.6%), v9 4,967 of 5,320 (93.4%), v7 4,941 of 5,276 (93.7%), hdae5000 296 of 335 (88%). v142 is at 12.3% and table_data at 10.2%. Counting all routine-like entry labels (a call target, or the first label after an unconditional ret/jp/jr), v10 has 16,201 of 18,047 without a header. Examples checked by hand: NoteMap_LookupAndAllocVoice, AccStyle_DetectChanges and NoteOn_VoiceLookupAndAssign have none. v10 call targets without headers by subsystem: sequencer 2,069, audio 731, ui 424, display 343, demo 228, midi 218, boot 181, storage 80, file_io 65. No existing metric (semantic_score, the census) measures this, so it has never shown in the badges.
top_gaps.suggested_approach: Write a header for each call target that states its purpose, its arguments and return registers (read from caller set-up and callee use), the RAM it touches, and its callees. Do v10 first, then run gap 2's propagation to carry the headers to v9 and v7. Add a 'header coverage' metric (the rule in label_quality.py) to semantic_score.py or a sibling script, so progress is measured and ratchets.
top_gaps.est_effort: large: about 4,400 headers in v10 and about 300 in hdae5000. At roughly 30-50 headers per agent-hour, about 100+ agent-hours
top_gaps.parallelizable_units: One unit per .s file. top_gaps.suggested_approach: Write a mechanical propagator, a sibling of scripts/renaming/harmonize_version_labels.py and scripts/tools/carry_trailing_comments.py. For each v10 label with a header block, find the same label in v9/v7. If the instruction body up to the next non-local label is textually identical, insert the header block. result.summary:
The KN5000 trees have no LABEL_xxxxxx, sub_ or loc_ labels left, and the ELF name component is 95-100% semantic (v10 96.30%, v7 95.24%, v142 99.41%, hdae5000 99.97%). The remaining quality debt is mostly documentation and symbolization, not naming:
- **Routine headers:** about 83% of v10 call targets have no header comment (4,397 of 5,320). v9 and v7 are worse (93%), partly because 944 and 784 v10 headers were never propagated to them.
- **Numeric RAM operands:** 29,044 operands in v10 still address RAM by number, across 3,471 addresses. The top 1,000 addresses cover 74% of the references.
- **Placeholder names:** about 1,530 generic or positional labels per v10/v9 tree, against 2,671 in v7. 205 of them can be fixed now, because pending naming proposals are already written.
- **HD-AE5000:** 1,164 assembler-local labels named only by address are invisible to semantic_score, and 296 of its 335 call targets have no header.
- **Non-C verbatim .incbin:** v7 6,591 B and table_data 318,468 B (six FTBMP BMPs). Every other KN5000 tree is 0.
- **Data documented by name only (KNOWN-B):** v10 74,701 B, v7 103,312 B, table_data 22,503 B. Self-admitted research targets total 69,368 B.
- **C struct fields:** about 1,384 placeholder fields per maincpu tree. naka_sequencer_channels.c is worst, with 337.
- **.byte between instructions:** v10 has 160 B after fall-through instructions (likely code) plus 2,994 B after terminators (likely unlabelled data). v7 has 1,480 B and 4,741 B.

The best-value order:
1. A mechanical propagation of v10 headers to v9/v7. It is cheap and enforces existing policy.
2. Header writing per file, starting with sequencer (2,069 call targets) and audio (731).
3. Naming RAM addresses by reference count, split into address-range lanes.
4. Applying the pending proposals and naming the generic labels per file.
5. Catching v7 up: bitmaps, transplants and .Lc_ locals.
6. Mechanical renaming of the HD-AE5000 locals.

All work units are per file or per address range and are independent. Only the rename-apply and harmonize steps must run serially.
result.measurement_method:
Nothing in the repo was written. All tools ran at HEAD 14aec1197.

**Repo tools**
- `python3 scripts/analysis/kn5000_source_coverage.py` (stdout only): per-image asm, typed, clang and verbatim bytes.
- `python3 scripts/analysis/kn5000_verbatim_list.py v7/maincpu` and `... table_data`: per-.incbin debt.
- Classification of each `.incbin` by summing its offset/length with `kn5000_source_coverage.INC` / `classify_incbin` imported in Python: v10 roundtrip 861,232 B over 9,963 directives, clang 9,270 B.
- `TMPDIR=<scratch> python3 scripts/analysis/data_range_census.py --images v10,v9,v7,v142,subboot,tabledata,customdata,hdae5000 --json <scratch>/drc.json --targets 40`. It mirrors and links in a tempdir under TMPDIR. All 8 images were inert and reconciled. Per-file KNOWN-B / UNKNOWN / embedded-in-code figures come from aggregating drc.json regions.
- `semantic_score.names(key)` and `semantic_score.c_fields`, imported (no `main()`, so no badge writes). These use the existing `rebuilt_ROMs/*.elf`, which predate commits a5220750d and d8574de89. I did not rebuild.

**My scratch scripts** (`/home/fsanches/compartilhado/tmp/technics-audit-quality-kn5000/`; they read .s files as latin-1 bytes)
- `label_quality.py` → `lq.json`.
  - Labels are column-0 `name:`. They are classified with semantic_score's CONTINUATION, POSITIONAL and GENERIC regexes, except that `.L` locals are positional only when they match `^\.L[A-Za-z]*_?[0-9a-f]{4,6}$`.
  - A code label is one whose next statement is an instruction (not a directive or a data macro).
  - A routine is a non-local code label that is a call/calr target in the same image tree, or follows an unconditional ret/jp/jr or data.
  - A label has a header when the nearest non-blank line above it starts with `;`.
  - Spot-checked by hand: NoteMap_LookupAndAllocVoice, AccStyle_DetectChanges and NoteOn_VoiceLookupAndAssign have none. AcIndexEditSwProc_OnDownStyle has a header in v10 but not in v9.
- `byte_in_code_split.py`: `.byte` runs whose neighbouring statements are both instructions (macro invocations excluded), split by whether the previous instruction is an unconditional terminator.
- `numeric_mem_refs.py`: `\((0xN|ddd+)(:8|:16|:24)?\)` operands in instruction lines, bucketed SFR (<0x100), RAM (<0x400000) and high.

**Other checks**
- Cross-version sync: set differences of no-header names between trees, intersected with v10's label set.
- `command grep -rhoE '^LABEL_[0-9A-Fa-f]{6}:'` and `'^(sub|loc|unk)_'` return 0 in every KN5000 tree.

**Caveats**
- [INFERENCE] Bytes after a fall-through instruction are presumed to be unspelled code. That presumption was checked on a sample, not on every run.
- The `_HHHH` positional rule has some false positives, e.g. RhythmMidi_CC7E.
- Per the global rule, the scratch scripts should be harvested into `~/compartilhado/research-scratch` (`./harvest.sh`). That is a git repo, so I left it for the next, non-read-only phase.

result.measurement_method:
Everything was read-only. Scratch scripts and outputs are in /home/fsanches/compartilhado/tmp/technics-audit-quality-wsa1/; I did not harvest them into research-scratch, because this phase is read-only.

1. **Unrated names.** names.py imports scripts/analysis/semantic_score.py (its CONTINUATION/POSITIONAL/GENERIC regexes) and runs llvm-nm --defined-only on wsa1/rebuilt_ROMs/wsa1_prom_{a,b,c,d}.llvm.elf. It reproduces semantic-score.json exactly (prom_a 5516/867/625/105 and so on). Each symbol is mapped to its defining file by scanning every wsa1 .s/.inc for `name:` or `.set name,` (as bytes). final.py sorts names into families (sub_ regex, T_ regex, DL prefixes, a Kind-word list, and whether the hex suffix equals the symbol's own address) and splits code from data by each label's first statement.
2. **Continuation breakdown.** Regex on the `__HEX` / `__word` / `_Skip` forms over the same ELF symbols.
3. **Callers.** callers.py collects call/calr/jp/jr/jrl operands per enclosing non-continuation label, then resolves the `T_X: jp Y` thunks. "Named caller" means any caller that is not sub_, OldCopy_ or T_XXXXXX. Data-pointer references are not seen, hence the "no direct caller" bucket.
4. **Headers.** headers2.py treats a code routine as a column-0 label whose first statement is an instruction and that does not match CONTINUATION. The header size is the number of consecutive `;` lines directly above, allowing one blank line, which is wave7_documentation_metrics.py's convention. The 1,970 prom_b `T_` slots are excluded. I also ran `python3 wsa1/notes/wave7_documentation_metrics.py`: content/framed/sub_ were prom_a 6130/600/125, prom_b 11531/1710/272, prom_c 1202/409/171, kernel 37/0/11.
5. **Bytes.** `TMPDIR=<scratch> python3 scripts/analysis/data_range_census.py --images prom_a,prom_b,prom_c,prom_d --json drc.json --targets 40`. Its not-understood totals match semantic-score.json (24,500 / 74,123 / 10,409 / 1,096). I also ran `python3 wsa1/scripts/analysis/source_coverage.py`.
6. **Style and symbolization.** style.py and inline `command grep -c -P` counts: `(0x...)` memory operands, `ld xRR,0x00Fxxxxx`, decimal immediates of 5+ digits, `.byte` lines, `.L` definitions, space or tab after the mnemonic, and cross-image `.set` lines.
7. **Macros.** I counted the m_/mx_/md_ invocations. macro_native3.py takes each prom_b macro line's trailing unidasm text, adds `:16`/`:24` from the macro's width argument, assembles it one line at a time with /home/fsanches/compartilhado/llvm-project/build/bin/llvm-mc (tlcs900_backend@a3a81863f87d), and compares against wsa1/original_ROMs/wsa1_prom_b.ic13 at the line's address.
8. **Naming pilot.** Proposals were counted from wsa1/notes/naming-pilot-2026-10-06/proposals_*.json: 1,120 named, 115 refused, 107 of the refused still sub_.
9. **Stale doc labels.** Backticked identifiers in README, HANDOFF and GAPS were checked against the ELF symbol sets and the source label index.

[INFERENCE] items:
- The prom_a macro native-respell rate, because prom_a's comments carry bytes but no mnemonic text.
- The family boundaries for 'semantic prefix + address' versus 'type-only'. They come from a hand-made vocabulary of kind words, so they are approximate to within tens of names.
